spans.s:
सृप् सृप् (connected with rt. सृ), cl. 1.
P. सर्पति (ep. also A. -ते), ससर्प (1st
du. ससृपिव), सर्प्स्यति or स्रप्स्यति, असृपत्,
असार्प्सीत् or अस्राप्सीत्, सर्प्तुम् or स्रप्तुम्, to
creep, crawl; to go, move: Pass. सृप्यते, Aor.
असर्पि: Caus. सर्पयति, -यितुम्, Aor. असीसृपत्
or अससर्पत्, to cause to creep, cause to go, &c.:
Desid. सिसृप्सति: Intens. सरीसृप्यते, सरीसर्प्ति;
[cf. Gr. ἕρπ-ω, ἑρπ-ύζ-ω, ἑρπ-ετό-ν, ἕρπ-η(τ)-ς,
Σαρπηδών, (according to some also) ῥέπ-ω, &c.: Lat.
serp-o, serp-en(t)-s, serp-ula, Pro-serp-ina (?),
rep-o (probably for srep-o): Old Germ. slich, ‘to
creep;’ (according to some also) slif for silf, ‘to
glide;’ Mod. Germ. schleife: Angl. Sax. slipan:
Lith. slenkiu, ‘to creep;’ reptoju, ‘to creep with
hands and feet:’ Hib. sleagaim, ‘to sneak.’]
सृप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, crept, crawled; gone, going.
सृप्ति, इस्, f. creeping, crawling; going, moving.

सृप्त्वा, ind. having crept or crawled; having
gone.

सृप्र, अस्, आ, अम्, creeping, going, proceeding,
gliding, (Sāy. = सर्पण-शील, प्रसृत); (अस्), m.
the moon.
—सृप्र-करस्न, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. one
whose hands are extended or mighty, (Sāy. = प्र-
सृत-बाहु.)
—सृप्र-दानु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. con-
stantly giving, (Sāy. = अविच्छेदेन धनानि प्र-
यच्छत्, Ṛg-veda

); (perhaps according to
some) possessed of flowing rain.
—सृप्र-भोजस्,
आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. conferring extended enjoyment.
—सृप्र-वन्धुर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (according to
some) having a wide fore part.
सृपाट सृपाट, अस्, m. a kind of measure.
सृपाटिका, f. the beak of a bird.

सृपाटी, f. a kind of measure; (according to
Śabda-k.) = रक्त-धारा.
